A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable text, equations, figures, and appendices. The original framework, simulations, and proofs can be matched reliably; v3 adds information-bottleneck background and Appendix G.

before.justification: v1 reports original GMM simulations, including KL Gap measurements under varying component counts in Section 4.4 and Figure 4, with repeated simulations documented in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the GMM simulations and adds original Dolly-15K experiments involving GPT-2 fine-tuning, synthetic-data statistics, and generator comparisons in Appendix G and Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: The prompt-conditioned synthetic-data generation framework, synthetic factors, and reverse-bottleneck formulation are retained. Appendix G instantiates this framework using standard in-context learning and fine-tuning, without introducing a new generation or training algorithm.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only simulated Gaussian-mixture data. Appendix G adds English instruction-following experiments using Dolly-15K and generated instructions, substantially extending coverage to real text and language-model post-training.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained anchor-versus-synthetic GMM comparison, Table 1 introduces unfine-tuned and real-data-fine-tuned GPT-2 controls. Table 4 compares GPT-4o with Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct as generators, reporting generation failure for the 1B model.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces an 80:20 Dolly-15K split, 3/10/20-example prompts, 20-epoch GPT-2 fine-tuning, reference-assisted Llama-3.1-Nemotron-70B judging, and softmax-normalized ratings. HSIC and semantic entropy provide additional evaluation measures. The original GMM protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test how prompt example counts affect downstream ratings and information-related measures, and how generator choice affects output quality. Appendix G.4 adds instruction-following failure analysis and examples of repetitive Llama-3.2-3B output. The original GMM component sensitivity analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Appendix G.3 adds HSIC and semantic entropy as statistical proxies for mutual information and dataset entropy. The GMM's 100-round averaging, resampling, and standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged. No repeated-run counts, seeds, or uncertainty estimates are reported for the new language-model results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 add substantial new results. Table 1 reports normalized ratings of 0.1863, 0.1965, and 0.2015 for 3/10/20-example synthetic-data conditions, versus 0.1409 for base GPT-2 and 0.2745 for real-data fine-tuning. New HSIC, entropy, and generator-failure findings supplement unchanged GMM results; these are new experiments rather than cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 removes the explicit description of the prompt transformation as reversible, although Appendix C still assumes reversibility for its inverse-transformation derivation. The principal bounds and proofs remain unchanged. New Appendix A.2 mainly formalizes standard information-bottleneck background.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and Section 5 retain the same central claims about distributional modeling, the reverse bottleneck, information gain, and GGMI. The new experiments provide supporting evidence without redefining these main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 changes the explanation of faithfulness from anchor–parameter conditional entropy H(Sanchor|W) to entropy reduction Delta H. Appendix G adds interpretations linking HSIC and semantic entropy to diversity and faithfulness, explains prompt-size effects, and identifies sufficient instruction-following capability as a practical requirement.

D1.justification: Appendix G supplies full generation and evaluation prompts, retained dataset fields, model identifiers, the data split, and the fine-tuning duration. The advertised code link changes from an anonymous repository to an author-hosted GitHub repository. Synthetic-data quantities and detailed estimator and optimization settings remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations supporting Dolly, Alpaca, the newly used models and judging procedure, HSIC, and semantic entropy. The main related-work organization and positioning of the reverse-bottleneck contribution remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. Local edits shorten related-work and transition paragraphs and clarify synthetic factors. Appendix A gains subsections, Appendix G is added, and the header, affiliations, and acknowledgments are updated.

P2.justification: Appendix G introduces a substantial new set of displays: four result tables, boxed generation and evaluation prompts, and boxed failure examples. The original five figures are retained, with surrounding text and page flow adjusted.

improvement.justification: Appendix G provides a useful empirical bridge beyond v1's GMM-only evidence, adding real-text experiments, generator failure cases, and inspectable prompts. The improvement is limited by missing uncertainty estimates and important training and estimator details. Section 5 also retains the statement that real-world LLM validation was unavailable, leaving the new evidence poorly integrated with the paper's conclusion.
